clue.text: Cleaner takes one inside to see the president

indicators.note: the cleaner takes something in, so her letters will hold another piece
inside says where the cleaner takes the numeral: within her own letters

parts.note: a charwoman is a woman paid to clean houses or offices
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cleaner brings a friend along to visit the head of the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who presides over a meeting or board is its chair, so a president in that sense.

clue.text: MFHs who find the best of the pack?

definitions.meaning: MFH stands for Master of Foxhounds, the person heading a hunt

definitions.text: who find the best of the pack
definitions.meaning: recruitment agents who pick out the top candidates from a crowd of applicants

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated answer splits as the heads of hunts; whole, it names executive recruiters, and 'the pack' plays on hounds and on a field of job seekers.
explanation.definitionFit: Masters of foxhounds lead hunts, and recruitment agents poach the top talent for companies.

clue.text: Repeatedly I caught antelope in interior of Northern island

indicators.note: in interior says the antelope goes into the middle of the doubled pair
Repeatedly says the pair of pieces before it is written out twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A hunter keeps catching antelope deep inside some island up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubling I and C gives ICIC; ELAND goes in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to Iceland, the large island in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Extremely undisciplined writer's given time

parts.note: Oscar Wilde is the writer; his possessive gives the letters of his name plus S

explanation.surface: A writer known for misbehaving is given a prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at Oscar Wilde's prison sentence; 'given' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective meaning unruly is the most unruly of all.

clue.text: Mother reversing when on a demonstration run gets wildly excited

indicators.note: reversing says the word for mother is to be read backwards

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, as in horse breeding
as means when, as in 'as I left'
a march is a protest demonstration
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: A mother runs backwards during a protest march and becomes frantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' tempts MA, but the animal-breeding word is the one that gets turned round by 'reversing'; 'on' and 'gets' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares crazed behaviour to hares boxing and leaping in their spring breeding season.

clue.text: Take-home business required computer system

parts.note: take-home pay is net pay, after deductions
work is one's business or occupation

explanation.surface: A firm that operates from home needs a computer system.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked computers sharing data and resources form one connected system of machines.

clue.text: Not all bound over can be set free

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A court order binding someone over still lets them walk out of the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie or unfasten something is to release it from what holds it.

clue.text: Clear a name when upset in unsuccessful position

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the run of pieces is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: to rid a place is to clear it

explanation.surface: Someone tries to clear their name but ends up in a losing spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' turns RIDAN round, giving NADIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of fortune is where a failing person ends up.

clue.text: At one time university carried little weight

indicators.note: carried says the phrase for formerly bears the university abbreviation within it

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly

explanation.surface: In the past the college lugged around only a light load.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of weight a sixteenth of a pound, and figuratively a tiny amount.

clue.text: Described the beautiful French diamonds

parts.note: la belle is French for the beautiful (woman)
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A gossip writer describes the glamorous French woman's jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag something with a name or category is to characterise it.

clue.text: What Achilles had to watch over?

definitions.meaning: the Achilles ... is the cord above the heel, his famous weak spot
to ... is an old phrase for waiting upon or looking after someone

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into TEND ON, meaning to attend upon someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The heel cord is named after the hero, and the split phrase means to look after.

clue.text: Idiomatic expression that is right in period

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for right within the word for a period

parts.note: a phase is a period or stage

explanation.surface: A turn of phrase is correct for its era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link here, not IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of words used together, often with a set meaning, is a phrase in grammar.

clue.text: Shaped block of sandalwood, perhaps?

parts.note: a foot-shaped former kept in footwear to hold its shape, with 'sandalwood' read as the wood inside a sandal

explanation.definitionFit: The device is a wooden or plastic foot shape put into footwear to stop it losing shape.

clue.text: Jumbo could be grounded following its report

definitions.text: Jumbo could be grounded following its report

parts.words: Jumbo could be grounded following its report
parts.note: reads as a jumbo jet grounded after an incident report, but means a large animal felled by the bang of a heavy rifle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests a jumbo jet and 'report' an inquiry; the report is a gunshot and the jumbo an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A large-calibre rifle made for big game, whose shot can bring down the largest land animal.

clue.text: Girl I aim to embrace

indicators.note: to embrace says the word for aim wraps its arms round the I

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl sets out with the goal of giving someone a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as of the writer Enid Blyton.

clue.text: Watch the enemy observer

parts.note: time is the enemy, as the saying goes
a keeper of rules is one who observes them

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the spy from the opposing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or wristwatch is a device for keeping time.

clue.text: Make space to move below at sea by lifting berth

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of below are jumbled
lifting in a down clue says the word for berth is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to berth a ship is to moor it

explanation.surface: A sailor clears room below decks by raising a bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns BELOW into ELBOW; 'lifting' turns MOOR into ROOM. 'Make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Room to stretch out one's arms means enough freedom to act or manoeuvre.

clue.text: After this, the French got excited about nothing

indicators.note: about says the jumble goes round the letter for nothing
got excited means stirred up, so the letters of the French are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are jumbled
O, the shape of zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: From then on the French became worked up over trifles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got excited' jumbles THEFRENCH into HENCEFRTH; 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means from this time on, the period following now.

clue.text: Platform's warning to political leader

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning cry
taken as written

indicators.note: leader says take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A stage or podium is where a warning is issued to a party boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Golfers shout 'fore' to warn others of a ball in flight. The 's of the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretop is the platform at the top of a ship's foremast.

clue.text: Regular takes a little port outside

indicators.note: outside says the port's letters wrap round the phrase for a little

parts.note: Hue is a port city in Vietnam
a bit means a little

explanation.surface: A regular drinker has a small glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the wine, but it is the Vietnamese city Hue; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual visitor to a place, such as a regular at a bar.

clue.text: Decorative inlay in nave reflected light, initially

indicators.note: reflected says the word for a wheel's centre is mirrored, read right to left

parts.note: the nave of a wheel is its hub

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of light

explanation.surface: A church nave has ornamental inlay catching the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nave' suggests a church; here it is a wheel's centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Buhl is brass or tortoiseshell inlay work on furniture, named after the cabinetmaker Boulle.

clue.text: Piano in his room could be one just like another

indicators.note: in places the piano abbreviation within the jumble
could be says the letters of his room may be rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are jumbled
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano in his bedroom might be identical to another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' jumbles HISROOM into ISOMORH; 'in' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In science, an isomorph is a thing having the same form or structure as another.

clue.text: Fish with a line that's the best available

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Catching a fish with rod and line is as good as it gets.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect or the model to aim at is the finest one could want.

clue.text: People drawn inside by very large signs

indicators.note: drawn inside by says people are pulled into the letters for very large

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
men means people, as in men at work

explanation.surface: Crowds are attracted by huge billboards.
explanation.definitionFit: Portents are indications of what will happen in future.

clue.text: Book overdue for submitting

parts.note: owing means unpaid and overdue

explanation.surface: A library book is late being handed back in.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding or bending to another's will, as in bowing to pressure.

clue.text: Players are told to go off in this direction

definitions.text: Players are told to go off in this direction

parts.words: Players are told to go off in this direction
parts.note: a stage direction in a script, the Latin word telling the actors that they all leave

explanation.walkthrough: 'direction' reads as a compass point but is a stage direction; 'Players' are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage instruction meaning 'they go out', telling actors to leave the stage.

clue.text: Notwithstanding, Hugh… just breaks into singer's finale

indicators.note: breaks into says Hugh's letters burst into the singer's word, at its finale, splitting round its last letter

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hugh nonetheless butts in on the vocalist's closing number.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh breaks into ALTO at its finale: his name splits round the final O, giving ALT + H-O-UGH. 'just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjunction meaning in spite of the fact that, the same sense as despite.

clue.text: Luxurious boozer

definitions.meaning: rich and luxurious, as in plush surroundings

explanation.definitionFit: Lush describes rich, opulent growth or comfort, and slang uses it for a habitual drunk.

clue.text: Point in publicity work is promotion to office

indicators.note: in places the compass point within the run of the other pieces

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
to work is to ferment, as yeast does
E is a point of the compass, east

explanation.surface: A point made in advertising work is about getting a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancement to a higher rank or position, especially in the church.
